facts.raw_span: bilateral photophobia and decreased vision
CD4 count was 24 cells/mm3
HIV RNA level was 175,000 copies/mL
pruritic back rash of crusting erythematous plaques
uncorrected visual acuity was hand motions in both eyes
intraocular pressures were 14 and 9 mm Hg in the right and left eye, respectively
corneal stromal haze, 3+ anterior chamber cell
vitreous cell and haze obscuring retinal vascular details
Cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay: positive
Rapid plasma reagin testing: 1:64 titer
interface dermatitis with spirochetes evident upon hematoxylin-eosin staining
Aqueous fluid from both eyes negative for herpetic viral DNA by PCR

concepts.why: Positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and rapid plasma reagin testing suggest syphilis, which can cause uveitis, especially in the context of a pruritic back rash and low CD4 count.
Low CD4 count and high HIV RNA level increase the risk of uveitis in HIV patients, which is supported by the presence of corneal stromal haze and vitreous cell and haze.

Positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and rapid plasma reagin testing suggest syphilis, which can cause chorioretinitis, especially in the context of a pruritic back rash and low CD4 count.
Low CD4 count and high HIV RNA level increase the risk of retinitis in HIV patients, which is supported by the presence of vitreous cell and haze obscuring retinal vascular details.

Positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and rapid plasma reagin testing suggest syphilis, which can cause optic neuritis, especially in the context of a pruritic back rash and low CD4 count.
Low CD4 count and high HIV RNA level increase the risk of neuroretinitis in HIV patients, which is supported by the presence of decreased vision and hand motions in both eyes.

Positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and rapid plasma reagin testing suggest syphilis, which can cause panuveitis, especially in the context of a pruritic back rash and low CD4 count.
Low CD4 count and high HIV RNA level increase the risk of posterior uveitis in HIV patients, which is supported by the presence of corneal stromal haze and vitreous cell and haze.

Positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and rapid plasma reagin testing suggest syphilis, which can cause intermediate uveitis, especially in the context of a pruritic back rash and low CD4 count.
Low CD4 count and high HIV RNA level increase the risk of anterior uveitis in HIV patients, which is supported by the presence of corneal stromal haze and vitreous cell and haze.
It explains the intraocular pressures and negative herpetic viral DNA PCR results in the context of syphilitic infection.

frontier_selector.rationale: Positive Cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and Rapid plasma reagin testing, along with interface dermatitis and spirochetes on skin lesion histopathology, strongly support syphilis as the underlying cause, and the eye findings are consistent with panuveitis.
